findings.title: Resolve target ancestors before allowing assembly writes
findings.trigger: Create a directory symlink (Linux) or junction (Windows) inside a disposable workspace that points to a sibling directory. Set --target to alias-outside/new-platform, where new-platform does not exist.
findings.observed: exit 0; base.txt and overlay.txt are written outside the chosen workspace. Pointing alias-input to 00-core similarly writes into preserved historical inputs.
findings.rootCause: resolveBeneath checks lexical paths only. The target realpath check runs only when the final target exists, so mkdirSync follows an existing linked ancestor. Reserved paths are compared using the lexical first segment.
findings.requestedChange: Validate every existing ancestor using lstat/realpath before creation or removal; reject symlink/junction traversal (or enforce canonical containment and canonical reserved-input exclusion). Apply equivalent source-root checks where the same helper is used. Cover nonexistent descendants, outside links and aliases into preserved directories with regression tests asserting zero writes.
findings.scope: Reproduced with verifier-owned synthetic fixture directories only. Linux symlink behavior inferred from the code path; Windows junction exploit directly observed.

findings.title: Assembler tests assume Unix symlink and executable-bit behavior
findings.observed: One fixture cannot create /etc/passwd symlink on native Windows (EPERM); another expects chmod to make Git index mode 100755, but Windows records 100644. These explain 2 of 3 local failures, rather than demonstrating Linux failures.
findings.requestedChange: Use portable fixture symlinks/junctions where available and set intended fixture Git executable modes explicitly; report unsupported platform prerequisites truthfully. Keep this separate from the confirmed V1 security failure.

findings.title: Inherited Windows conformance failure remains
findings.observed: dummy-ok C-004 rejects valid evidence paths; 527/528 conformance tests pass. This behavior is byte-identical to the historical platform and assigned to S2-01; not an S1-01 regression.
